paragraphs: Brent Council fosters for children in the borough's care, and the services listed above also cover Brent. Enquiries to the council are handled by Foster with West London, the recruitment hub shared by eight west London councils, and the council says it wants to recruit more carers for Brent's children.

The council has been rebuilding its own fostering service. A report to its corporate parenting committee in February 2024 recorded that the number of council fostering households fell by 39% between 2017-18 and 2022-23, and set out a revised offer for carers. Allowances then rose in two steps, the second in April 2025. The council now pays a combined weekly allowance and fee of between £235.67 (a child up to 4, level 1 carer) and £502.43 (a young person of 16 or over, level 3 carer). Carers also get a laptop or tablet, a Blue Light Card, birthday, holiday and festival payments, help with a bed, cot or car seat, Fostering Network membership, 24-hour phone support, free therapeutic support and the Mockingbird peer-support scheme.

To foster for the council you need to be at least 21 and live in Brent or a neighbouring borough, with a spare bedroom (or room for a cot, for a baby up to two). You can rent or own your home, be single or in a couple, and keep working if your job leaves time for school runs and appointments. The council's assessment takes up to six months, ending with a fostering panel.
Compare the council with two or three of the services above, and see the Harrow, Ealing and London pages if you live near the borough's edge.
